label: Absolute URI
definition: A URI that already has a scheme. A reference without one is rejected, and RFC 3986 relative-reference resolution is not this package's job.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Scheme dispatch
definition: The core checks scheme grammar, compares schemes case-insensitively, and hands the original URI to the resolver registered for that scheme.
:LABEL: Concept

label: URI fragment
definition: The fragment is split off before dispatch and is never an identifier. Resolvers must not turn it into a path, a key, or a selection.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Opaque payload
definition: When a resolver marks its payload opaque, logs, errors, reprs, and temporary paths show the scheme plus a digest, not the payload.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Redaction
definition: Secrets, credential-bearing backend errors, and opaque URI payloads are stripped before they are logged or chained onto an exception.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Scheme naming
definition: A private scheme uses a reversed domain the deployer controls. A short unregistered name is not a conforming choice.
:LABEL: Concept

label: URI equivalence
definition: The core case-folds the scheme and does not otherwise normalize. Percent-encoding, dot segments, and default ports stay the resolver's problem.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Scheme definition
definition: Every scheme a deployment registers needs a page in SCHEMES.md stating syntax, operations, and security before the scheme is usable.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Public resolve API
definition: Context.resolve is the real entry point. The module-level resolve function is a process-default convenience that library code should not rely on.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resolve context
definition: The context owns resolver lifetime, the secrets provider, the memory limit, and session reuse. Closing it invalidates resources it produced.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resolved resource
definition: The object a resolver returns. It keeps the caller's URI and the concrete URI, and it is bound to the context that created it.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resource info
definition: A cheap description filled in at resolve time: kind, existence, and optional size or shape. It must not pull the bulk bytes.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Tier 0 baseline
definition: info and materialize are present on every resource. Policy may make them fail, but it may not hide them.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Materialize
definition: Delivery of a resource into a file or memory destination. Resolve itself does not download or convert; this call does.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Canonical media type
definition: The resolver names the byte encoding for a structured resource. The core does not invent one.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Form
definition: What the caller wants back from memory delivery: a backend-native object, bytes, or an optional array or table.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Materialized result
definition: The value plus enough URI and strategy metadata for an outside provenance layer to record what was staged.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Materialization strategy
definition: A short token on the result that says whether the backend did the work, the bytes were sliced locally, or a reference was returned.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Strict efficiency
definition: When the context flag is set, a delivery that would read the whole object and slice it locally is refused before the transfer starts.
:LABEL: Concept

label: File destination
definition: A caller-chosen path. Successful delivery leaves that path in place, written via a temporary name and an atomic replace.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Reference policy
definition: Copy is the default. A link or in-place path is returned only when the caller asked, and failure cleanup must not delete that source.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Memory destination
definition: An in-memory delivery in a chosen form, bounded by the destination or context byte limit.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Selection
definition: The only portable subsetting in the baseline is numpy basic indexing, plus a column list for tables. Anything else is not a core query language.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Native selection
definition: A wrapper that passes a backend-specific query through untouched. Using it means the caller has accepted protocol coupling.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Tier 1 facet
definition: An optional declared interface borrowed from an existing library, so generic code can do more than fetch the whole object.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Stream facet
definition: A binary reader for resources that can be opened as a byte stream, including range reads where the backend supports them.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Array facet
definition: Shape, dtype, and numpy basic indexing on an array resource. Fancy indexing is not part of the facet.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Table facet
definition: Column names and an optional row count, with a read that can ask for a subset of columns.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Container facet
definition: Named children of a container, each itself a resolved resource. Keys are single path segments, not a path traversal API.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Tier 2 native pass-through
definition: Backend operations the wrapper does not rename or reinterpret. Callers who use them accept that the call is protocol-specific.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Capability
definition: supports is the one answer for what a resource can do. capabilities and attribute lookup report that same set.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Policy filtering
definition: A resolver may hide backend operations. That filter is a convenience in this process, not a security boundary.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resolver
definition: The plugin that interprets one scheme: sessions, credentials, info, and materialize. The core does not parse the scheme-specific part for it.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Registry
definition: The map from scheme to resolver. Two schemes may share a protocol and still point at different servers and credentials.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resolver plugin
definition: An installed distribution registers schemes through entry points. Those points are listed at import and imported on first use.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Namespace indirection
definition: A namespace URI asks which concrete URI an identifier maps to for this caller right now. That is not RFC 3986 reference resolution.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Namespace service
definition: A self-hosted POST /resolve endpoint. The process is urisolver's; the routing function is the deployer's.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Bespoke routing
definition: Persistent names stay small because the private routing rules live in the deployer's resolver, not in the core.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Secrets provider
definition: A get_secret lookup by id. The core never stores the values, and the resolver asks only for the id the catalog selected.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Error model
definition: Failures are typed by stage: bad URI, unknown scheme, access, namespace, materialize, selection, secrets, and plugins.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Async names
definition: aresolve and amaterialize are reserved so later async support does not fork the API. Sync callers do not need an event loop.
:LABEL: Concept

label: file scheme
definition: The built-in resolver for local paths: stat for info, a stream facet, and byte contents for memory delivery.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Tiled resolver
definition: An optional resolver that reads a Tiled node. The server address and the secret id come from the local resolution catalog.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Globus resolver
definition: An optional Transfer resolver for one collection path. File delivery is a copy; memory delivery stages through the catalog's staging collection.
:LABEL: Concept

label: CryoET example
definition: An example resolver for one public object on a CryoET Data Portal origin. The origin comes from the local resolution catalog. A .zarr path is an OME-Zarr multiscale array; an .mrc path is a file whose size comes from HEAD.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Resolution catalog
definition: A local YAML file that binds a scheme to a server, a secret id, and optional path-prefix overrides. Secret values are not in the file.
:LABEL: Concept

label: Conformance baseline
definition: A resolver-agnostic test suite shipped with the package. A plugin that does not pass it is not a conforming resolver.
:LABEL: Concept
